summary: vssadmin.exe ran a read-only 'list shadows' command, spawned by backup-agent.exe under the svc-backup service account on a file server. This looks like routine backup software checking existing shadow copies. Shadow copy enumeration can precede ransomware deletion, but nothing here shows deletion or other malicious behavior.

evidence.why: This is a read-only enumeration command, not 'delete shadows' or 'resize shadowstorage' that ransomware typically uses. However, enumeration alone can be attacker reconnaissance, so it is not fully conclusive.
A backup agent is an expected parent for VSS queries, which supports a benign backup workflow. The parent's legitimacy is not verified in the alert, so a masquerading binary cannot be ruled out.
A dedicated backup service account running a backup-related command is consistent with normal operations. Service accounts can be compromised, so this is supportive but not proof.
vssadmin.exe has a valid signature, indicating the genuine Windows binary rather than a tampered copy. Attackers often abuse legitimate signed tools, so this only rules out binary replacement.
A file server is a typical host for backup and shadow copy activity, but it is also a high-value ransomware target, so any follow-on VSS deletion should be watched.

recommended_action.detail: Close as expected backup activity after a quick check that backup-agent.exe is the approved binary and svc-backup runs this on a regular schedule (around 01:30 UTC). Escalate if vssadmin delete/resize commands or unusual activity from svc-backup appear on srv-file-02.
